anchors.assertion: Project root contains a README.md with instructions to install dependencies, run the app, and access the UI
Project contains a web frontend (HTML/JS or SPA framework) served by the app on the default HTTP port
Backend exposes RESTful API endpoints under /api/ prefix for note operations (create, read, update, delete, list)
Data persistence is implemented (file-based, SQLite, or any database); notes survive app restart
GET /api/notes returns a JSON array of all saved notes with id, title, content, template, and created_at fields
POST /api/notes creates a new note and returns the created note object with a non-empty id
GET /api/notes/:id returns the note with the given id, or 404 if not found
PUT /api/notes/:id updates an existing note and returns the updated note
DELETE /api/notes/:id removes the note and returns 204 No Content
The UI displays a list of saved notes and allows creating a new note
The UI allows editing an existing note and saving changes via the API
The UI includes a SOAP note template pre-populated in the note editor (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan sections)
Basic authentication is implemented (login/logout) and unauthenticated requests to /api/notes return 401
POST /api/notes with empty title and empty content returns 400 Bad Request, not 200
GET /api/notes/:id with non-numeric id returns 404 Not Found (not 500)
DELETE /api/notes/:id for a non-existent id returns 404 Not Found
PUT /api/notes/:id with mismatched URL id and body id returns 400 Bad Request
A test suite exists and `go test ./...` or equivalent runs without errors (exit code 0)
Tests cover POST /api/notes creating a note and GET /api/notes listing it
Tests cover 404 responses for GET /api/notes/:id with non-existent id and DELETE /api/notes/:id with non-existent id
Tests cover PUT /api/notes/:id updating a note and verifying the update persisted
No busy-wait loops or blocking sleep in request handlers; responses complete within 100ms under normal load
Note listing and creation do not scan or load all notes into memory for each request (applicable only if >100 notes)
